summary: Iter222 retested the iter221 caller ID fixes. All 3 fixes pass. (1) Bot hub nudge: the Starter+Pro user gets '+18336221103 … $45.00'; Starter-only gets $70.00; Business gets no nudge; the nudge is sent only once (bot e2e 19/19, including 2b which failed in iter221). (2) Web CallerIdUpsellCard: for Bob the CTA goes to /cloudivr/app/numbers/%2B18509558201?tab=billing&plan=business (the Pro number, not the replaced Starter) and the text reads 'for just $45'. With /numbers mocked to Starter-only, it shows $70 and targets the non-replaced +14062358695. Alice (Business) sees no card. (3) The manager list order matches the chips (most recently used first), and both reorder after a dry-run callback with showAs. Label and number are no longer truncated: the number shows in full and the label wraps onto its own line. Regression: pytest 19/19 (iter221 9, iter220 8, new iter222 2). Web UI checks pass: attest with label, chip 'TEST_Lbl · +num' shown first, rename and clear through the prompt, 911 blocked ('Emergency numbers can't be used as a caller ID.'), no 'logged' wording. NEW ISSUE: the dashboard card promises $45, but its CTA opens the general Billing upgrade, which quotes $101.25 for the same number. Details below.

minor.issue: The price-difference quote (diff=true → callerIdUpgradeQuote) is used only by /caller-ids/upgrade, which returns charge 45 for Bob's Pro. The billing-tab upgrade, /numbers/%2B18509558201/upgrade {plan:business}, returns charge 101.25 (Business $120 minus an $18.75 upgrade credit). The dashboard card's CTA leads to the second one.

ui_bugs.issue: The card says 'Upgrade to Business for just $45 — you pay only the price difference', but the CTA lands on the Billing tab (?tab=billing&plan=business). There, 'See price' shows 'Pay $101.25 now — includes a $18.75 upgrade credit…'. The user is promised $45 and quoted $101.25. Fix: when plan=business comes from the caller ID card (or always for business), use /caller-ids/upgrade or the diff quote in BillingTab; or make the CTA call /caller-ids/upgrade directly with a confirm step. The bot nudge quotes $45 too, so both channels disagree with the Billing tab.
The card renders before /public/catalog loads, so it briefly shows 'Upgrade to Business — you pay…' with no price, and the $45 appears a moment later. Minor flicker.

issues: Rename still uses the native window.prompt (carried over from iter221, not addressed).

action_items: Make the dashboard card's upgrade path charge the $45 price difference it promises. Today BillingTab (/numbers/:n/upgrade) quotes $101.25 for Bob's Pro +18509558201. Either point the CTA at the /caller-ids/upgrade quote+confirm flow, or apply the diff quote when upgrading to business from the card.
Optional: hide the card's price text (or the card) until the catalog has loaded, to avoid the flicker.
critical_code_review_comments: Banners.js eligible filter excludes replacedBy and isSubNumber but not on-hold or suspended numbers; the bot uses planLifecycle.onHold(n). A suspended Pro could be targeted on web, and its billing upgrade returns 409 'Restore this number first'.
There are two upgrade pricing models for the same plan change (diff vs credit). Users can get different prices depending on the entry point. Consider one rule.

success_rate.frontend: 90% (all 3 fixes verified; new mismatch between the card CTA and the Billing price)

Web: route.fetch() inside Playwright loses auth (returns 401), so mock /api/cloudivr-web/numbers with a static body to simulate Starter-only. Compare these two for the Pro number: POST /caller-ids/upgrade {} returns 45, POST /numbers/%2B18509558201/upgrade {plan:business} returns 101.25. Do NOT confirm, because Bob's wallet is $39.55.
rca of the issue: The card computes its price with the diff model (business minus the current plan price). Its CTA opens BillingTab, which POSTs /numbers/:n/upgrade. That call goes to upgradeNumber(..., diff=false) → computeUpgradeQuote, which uses the credit model. Only caller-ids.js /caller-ids/upgrade passes diff=true. Reproduce: log in as Bob, click the card's CTA, then click 'See price' → $101.25.
